extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and advanced students interested in analytic geometry and properties of plane quadrilaterals (readers of The Mathematician, 1847)
extracted.subtask_description: Derivations and enumerated geometric properties of a plane quadrilateral (inscribed and circumscribed conics, harmonic divisions, loci of centres, and centres of gravity constructions) using coordinates and conic-section analysis. Contains many labeled theorems/properties and constructive methods for centres of gravity and related derived figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conics through four points — classification by position of one point
rubrics_metrics.description: If one of four points is without the triangle formed by joining the other three, there can pass through the points an indefinite number of ellipses, an indefinite number of hyperbolas, and two parabolas; if the one point is within such triangle, hyperbolas only can pass through the given points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "[a) If one of four points be without the triangle formed by joining the other three, there can pass through the points y an indefinite number of ellipses, an indefinite number of hyperbolas, and two parabolas. If however, the point be within such triangle, hyperbolas only can pass through the given points." (Explanation given via sign choices of parameters A,B,C in general second-order equation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Chord-of-contact loci for fixed external point
rubrics_metrics.description: For a family of conic sections circumscribed to a given quadrilateral whose diagonals intersect in O, the points of contact corresponding to a fixed external point E all lie on the same straight line (OF); similarly the contacts for F lie on OE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: "If a series of conic sections he circumscribed to a given quadrilateral figure, whose diagonals intersect in O, and from E and F, the intersections of the two pairs of opposite sides, tangents be drawn, then will all the points of contact corresponding to the point E, lie in OF, and those corresponding to F, will lie in OE." (Derivation via chord-of-contact and algebraic identities.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagonals of circumscribed quadrilaterals concur at same point O
rubrics_metrics.description: For any number of second-order curves passing through the same four points A,B,C,D, the diagonals of all quadrilaterals circumscribed to those curves pass through the same point — the intersection O of the diagonals of the inscribed quadrilateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Stated as property (e); derived by combining tangent equations so absolute terms vanish.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersections of opposite sides of circumscribed figures lie on a fixed line EF
rubrics_metrics.description: The points of intersection of the opposite sides of the circumscribed quadrilaterals (the three pairs of opposite sides) all lie on the same straight line EF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Stated as property (d); shown by algebraic combination of side equations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonic division on lines determined by quadrilateral
rubrics_metrics.description: If four points A,B,C,D are joined pairwise forming six lines, and the intersections of opposite pairs are E,F and diagonals meet at O, then with respect to each of the six lines (produced if necessary) there will be four points of intersection at which each line is harmonically divided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "[e) If we join four given points A, B, C, D, taken in pairs, by six straight lines ... then with respect to each of the six lines (produced if necessary) there will be four' points of intersection, at which each of the lines will be harmonically divided." (Connects to chord-of-contact and polar properties.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Lines from intersection of tangents produce harmonic division on chord/contact
rubrics_metrics.description: If from the intersection of two tangents to a conic a line is drawn to meet the curve and the chord of contact, that line will be divided harmonically at the four points (the two contact points and the two curve intersections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: "(/) If from the intersection of two tangents to a conic section, a line be drawn to meet the curve and the chord of contact, this line will be divided harmonically at the four points." (Given as corollary/exercise.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus of centres of conics through four points — ellipse vs hyperbola
rubrics_metrics.description: The locus of centres of all conic sections passing through four given points is a hyperbola if one of the four points is outside the triangle formed by the other three; it is an ellipse if that point lies within the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "(g) If one of four points be without the triangle formed by joining the other three, the locus of the centres of all conic sections which pass through the given points is a hyperbola: if, however, that point be within such triangle, the locus is an ellipse." (Derived from elimination of parameter h.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate diameter directions of locus curve
rubrics_metrics.description: The locus curve (of centres) has three pairs of conjugate diameters parallel respectively to the three pairs of opposite sides: AB & CD, BC & AD, AC & BD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "(h) The curve (25) has three pairs of conjugate diameters parallel, respectively, to the sides AB, CD; BC, AD; AC, BD." (Follows because coefficient of xy in locus eqn is zero).

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle-points and diagonal-intersections lie on locus curve
rubrics_metrics.description: The intersections of the three pairs of opposite lines (including diagonals) and the middle points of the six lines (sides and diagonals) lie on the conic which is the locus of the centres of all conics through the four given points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "(k) If four given points, taken in pairs, be joined by six straight lines, the intersections of the three pairs of opposite lines ... and the middle points of the six lines, lie in the conic section which is the locus of the centres of all conic sections which pass through the four points." (Equations for middle points satisfy locus eqn.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Three lines joining midpoints concur at centre of locus curve
rubrics_metrics.description: The three straight lines which join the middle points of the opposite sides and of both diagonals intersect in the centre of the curve which is the locus of the centres of all conic sections through the quadrilateral's vertices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "(m) The three straight lines which join the middle points of the opposite sides and of both diagonals of a quadrilateral, intersect in the centre of the curve which is the locus of the centres ..." (Coordinates and intersection point given.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Four circumcircles of triangles formed by produced opposite sides meet in one point
rubrics_metrics.description: If the pairs of opposite sides of a quadrilateral are produced to meet and one describes a circle about each of the four triangles so formed, then the four circles meet in the same point P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "(w) If we produce the pairs of opposite sides AB, CD, and AD, BC, of a quadrilateral ABCD, till they intersect, and describe a circle about every one of the four triangles so formed, the four circles will intersect in the same point." (Equations (38),(39),(40) indicate intersection.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Centers of the four circumcircles lie on a circle through common point P
rubrics_metrics.description: The centres of the four circles mentioned above lie on another circle which also passes through the common intersection point P of the four circumcircles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "(p) The centres of the four circles lie in another circle which passes through P, the point common to all." (Stated without full derivation in article.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpendicular feet from common intersection P are collinear
rubrics_metrics.description: Perpendiculars from the common intersection point P to the sides AB, BC, CD, DA meet those sides in four points which are collinear (lie on the same straight line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "(jp) Perpendiculars from P on the sides AB, BC, CD, DA, intersect these sides in four points which range on the same straight line."

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of radii when quadrilateral cyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: When the four points A,B,C,D lie on the circumference of a circle, the difference of the squares of the radii of the first two of the four circumcircles equals the difference of the squares of the radii of the other two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "(q) When the four points A, B, C, D, lie in the circumference of a circle, the difference of the squares of the radii of the first two circles is equal to the difference of the squares of the radii of the other two." (Stated as a curiosity.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction method for centre of gravity via triangle centroids (EG,FH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction: draw the diagonals AC, BD and find the centroids E and F of triangles ABC and BCD; draw EG and FH parallel respectively to BD and AC; their intersection Q is the centroid (centre of gravity) of the whole quadrilateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original method (r): stepwise constructive recipe with coordinates given; useful for producing the centroid without calculus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate centroid construction using one-third offsets (parallelogram OQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction: draw diagonals AC, BD; set off on DC a segment equal to one third of the difference of OC and OA and on OD a part equal to one third of the difference of OD and OB; complete the parallelogram OQ — then Q is the centroid of the quadrilateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original method (s): attributed as known (Mechanics Magazine, Lady's Diary 1830); algebraic coordinates justify the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centroid by one triangle centroid and one-third of diagonal
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction: draw diagonals AC, BD, find centroid E of triangle ABC; draw EG parallel to BD and take EQ equal to one third of OD; then Q is the centroid of the quadrilateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original method (t): elegant practical method: EQ = (1/3)OD along line through E parallel to BD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centroid via bisectors of opposite sides and one-third ratio (P->Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction: bisect two pairs of opposite sides by lines meeting in P; join P to intersection O of diagonals; produce OP until the produced part PQ is one third of OP; then Q is the centroid of the quadrilateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original method (u): geometric construction based on coordinate relations; P is intersection of bisectors of opposite sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrilateral of triangle-centroids is similar and scaled by 1/3 with reversed position
rubrics_metrics.description: If one joins the centroids of the four triangles that pairwise compose the quadrilateral, the resulting quadrilateral is similar to the original, reversed in position, and its area equals one ninth of the original quadrilateral's area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "(r) If we join the centres of gravity of the four triangles which two and two compose a quadrilateral, we shall form another quadrilateral similar to the former, but reversed in position, and whose area is equal to one ninth of the original quadrilateral." (Coordinate derivation shows diagonals scaled by 1/3.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallelogram from centroids of diagonal-triangles — parallel to diagonals and area ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Joining centroids of the four triangles formed by the two diagonals (with vertex at intersection O) yields a parallelogram whose sides are parallel to the quadrilateral's diagonals; its area is two ninths of the original quadrilateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original properties (x),(z): construction KLMN is a parallelogram, sides parallel to AC,BD; area relation given as two ninths; coordinates explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterated centroid constructions produce sequence of similar quadrilaterals/parallelograms with geometric area ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: By iterating the process of forming quadrilaterals and parallelograms from centres of gravity of triangles (and middle points), one obtains a sequence of inscribed quadrilaterals/parallelograms whose areas form a geometric series (e.g., factors 1/9, 1/81, ...), with all diagonals intersecting on the same line OQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: "By continuing the process we get a series of parallelograms and inscribed quadrilaterals, the areas of the latter being denoted by the series ... where A is the area of the original quadrilateral." (Gives the multiplicative area ratios and notes the common line OQ.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle-point parallelogram and recursive similarity construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Joining middle points of adjacent sides of the original quadrilateral forms a parallelogram with sides parallel to diagonals; joining the points where the sides of this parallelogram cut the diagonals yields another quadrilateral similar to the original; repeating yields a family of similar figures whose diagonals all intersect on line OQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as further geometric relations and an exercise for the student; coordinates and prior results justify the claims.
